attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you drag the [set background color to] block inside the [on start] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Did you select a color for the background?

❓ Did you click ▶ to see the background color update?
steps.instructions:
Add a background color to this project!


Open the Scene code block menu, drag a [set background color to] block inside the [on start] container block, then click the gray bubble to select a color from the menu. 


Click ▶ under the MakeCode game console to see the color appear on the screen.

steps.hints: ❓ After clicking the gray box, did you select the Gallery tab from the top menu?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Did you drag the [set sprite to] block inside the [on start] container block?

❓ Did you click the gray box to select a sprite image?

❓ Did you explore the Gallery and select an image for the sprite?
steps.instructions:
Add a sprite to this project! A sprite is any character or object in MakeCode.


Open the Sprites code block menu and drag a [set sprite to] block inside the [on start] container block. Then click the gray box and select a sprite from the Gallery tab. 


Click ▶ to see your sprite appear on the screen!

steps.hints: ❓Did you drag the [set sprite position to] block underneath the [set sprite to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Did you drag the [set sprite position to] block inside the [on start] container block, underneath the [set sprite to] block?

❓ What do you think the [set sprite position to] block will do?
steps.instructions:
Add a block to move the sprite to a different position!


Open the Sprites code block menu and drag a [set sprite position to] block underneath the [set sprite to] block inside the [on start] container block.

steps.hints:
❓Did you try both larger and smaller values for the x and for the y to see how it changes the sprite’s position? 


﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Where do you want your sprite to appear on the screen?


Sensei Pro Tip:  

💡 Guide the ninja to notice that the x coordinate value range is 0-160, and the y coordinate value range is 0-120.

💡 Larger x values move the sprite to the right, and smaller x values move the sprite left. Larger y values move the sprite down, smaller y values move the sprite up.
steps.instructions:
Now, pick the sprite’s position!


Click in the white bubbles to change the x and y coordinate values.


The x value will move the sprite left or right, the y value will move the sprite up or down.


Click ▶ to see the position of your sprite.

steps.hints: ❓Did you drag the [sprite say] block underneath the [set sprite to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓What do you want your sprite to say?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Guide the ninja to notice that the order of the code blocks matters. Any block that refers to a sprite needs to come after its [set sprite to] block.
steps.instructions:
Make the sprite say something!


Open the Sprites code block menu and drag a [sprite say] block underneath the other blocks inside the [on start] block. Click in the white bubble and type something for the sprite to say. 


Click ▶ to see what the sprite says on screen.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of White Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about using code to create your first projects at Code Ninjas! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: The Journey Begins
badges.description: Use the MakeCode Arcade platform to code a project.

badges.title: Sprite Place at the Sprite Time
badges.description: Create a new sprite and set its position.

badges.title: Painter’s Palette
badges.description: Change the background color of a project.

badges.title: First Words
badges.description: Make a sprite say something on screen.

badges.title: Hearts, Smiles, and Bubbles, Oh My!
badges.description: Add screen effects to a project.

badges.title: Maestro
badges.description: Play a sound in a project.
